cues.en: All right.
In this lecture we are going to talk about origin time complexity.

Let's say in these numbers we want to find out number one.
So we know that it is located at the beginning of the array.
But if we are looking for, for example different number which is eight, we don't know where it is
located.
It is located at the end of the array.
So in this case linear search which is taking the on time complexity will not be beneficial.
We are going to approach this problem in an efficient way.
So to be able to find the number one, we are going to divide this array into two parts.
So if we divide it into two parts, we will have first part and second part.
And we know that the number one is located in the first part.
So this means that we don't need second part, so we can easily remove the second part and continue
our search in the first part.
Now one more time we are just going to repeat the process.
So in this case we are going to divide these numbers into two parts.

We will get rid of the second part.

So we're just going to remove this part.

So we are going to divide it into two parts.
And we don't need the second part.
And we are going to remove this part.
And we have successfully find the number one.
Now this technique is called divide and conquer.
And we are going to cover this in our upcoming lectures as well.
So this is very efficient way of finding the any given number in a sorted array.
So let's bring back everything.
Then I'm going to count the number of the steps that we went through to find the number one.
So in the first step we have divided this array into two parts and this is the first step.
Then in the second step we have divided it one more time.
Then in the third step we have divided it one more time.
So we need three steps to find out the number one.
And remember that we had eight items in the array.
So two to the third power equals eight.
So you might be interested that why we put over here two.
So we put two because every time we are dividing it into the two parts.
So if we put the number of the steps on the power of two it's going to be the eight.

So this is a very small array.
So it's going to be very easy to find the element in this array.
But the real power of this is when we get the very large numbers.
So let's say we have an expression like this.
So let's say this is the number of the elements that we have in our array.
So we want to find a particular number in this array.
So you can easily see that the number of the elements in this array is more than a million.

You will find that this is the 20.

and find something.
So this way using divide and conquer you will find that item in 20 steps.
So if you look at the analogy of the deck of cards.
So let's say we have ordered our deck of cards like this.
So in the first row we have diamonds, then we have clubs.
Then in the second part we have hearts and spades.
So let's say we want to find out ten hearts over here.
So if we approach the same problem by dividing the cards into two, it's going to be the same approach.
So we are dividing it by two.
Then we are going to concentrate on the second part.
We know that it is located in the second part.
Then we can continue to divide it one more time.
Then it's going to be lived only with the hearts.
Then we can continue to the hearts by dividing it one more time to the half, and continue until finding
the ten hearts.
So this is going to be the real life example of the logarithmic expression.
Now, if you look at the time complexity graph that we had before, in this case, the graph for the
logarithmic expression is going to be very flat.
So it's not going to be as flat as O1, but it is very flat and it is very efficient compared to O n
